subject.title: [Feature]: Cron should distinguish execution success from delivery failure and show warning instead of error

question: Should successful cron execution followed by failed delivery become a first-class `warning` run status, or should cron keep `status=ok` and have Control UI derive a warning presentation from delivery fields?
rationale: Both approaches solve the false execution-failure signal, but the choice changes persisted status semantics, Gateway validation, UI filters, backoff behavior, and external consumer expectations.

options.title: Use ok plus delivery fields
options.body: Keep primary run status as execution-only `ok` and render warning UI from `deliveryStatus`, `lastDeliveryError`, and diagnostics so the protocol enum does not expand.

options.title: Add first-class warning
options.body: Adopt `warning` as a persisted/API status after updating schema, storage readers, CLI/UI filters, plugin hooks, docs, and compatibility proof.

options.title: Keep delivery failures as errors
options.body: Retain current error semantics so delivery-target failures continue to drive `status=error`, backoff, and failure alerts.

recommendation.title: Use ok plus delivery fields
recommendation.body: Keep primary run status as execution-only `ok` and render warning UI from `deliveryStatus`, `lastDeliveryError`, and diagnostics so the protocol enum does not expand.

likelyOwner.reason: YuzuruS authored the merged adjacent delivery-status split and is the strongest history-linked owner for the status-versus-delivery contract tradeoff.
